name: Saint Lucia

findings.local_actor: Government of Saint Lucia; KLED (St. Lucia) Limited
findings.financier: CIFI (senior and subordinated loans); MIGA guarantee
findings.summary: A 2019 public-private partnership with KLED to replace streetlights also installs, operates and maintains up to about 970 CCTV cameras at over 300 sites island-wide; MIGA's disclosure names Dahua as the camera manufacturer.

sources.publisher: Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (World Bank Group)

findings.analyst_inference: The island-wide CCTV deployment is corroborated by two opened S1 sources on different hosts, but the Dahua attribution rests on MIGA alone; the government consultancy lists 'OLIX'-prefixed camera models without naming a manufacturer, which may be rebadged hardware. Pole follows the camera vendor per the equipment rule, though KLED (Irish-founded, BVI equity vehicle) operates the system. Tier 4: contract signed, financing closed, installation under supervision 2023-24; CIFI says the streetlights are operational but does not confirm the cameras are live. Project financing figures (MIGA up to US$11.7m guarantee; CIFI US$8.6m loans on US$10.3m cost) cover streetlights and CCTV together, so values left null.

findings.local_actor: Flow (Cable & Wireless Communications, Liberty Latin America)
findings.summary: Ericsson won a three-year managed-services deal to maintain the mobile core and radio equipment and run network operations for Flow's mobile networks in twelve northern Caribbean markets, including Saint Lucia.
findings.analyst_inference: Managed services, not confirmed equipment supply; the 2016 release does not name the radio/core vendor. The 2020 LLA release makes Ericsson LLA's sole mobile core vendor region-wide but does not name Saint Lucia, so it supports but does not corroborate. The 2016 contract was three years; still_current not confirmed, though the 2020 core deal suggests continuing Ericsson control of Flow's core. Digicel's vendor not established.

findings.controller: Government of Saint Lucia (Ministry of the Public Service)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of the Public Service, Information and Broadcasting
findings.summary: Taiwan grant-funded a government Multi-Channel Data Centre project for Saint Lucia, with a US$2.5m approved sum disbursed in tranches from 2013 and further Taiwanese funding handed over in 2017.
findings.analyst_inference: Government-owned facility, so domestic; Taiwan is financier only. Tier 4 as funds disbursed and a digitisation centre opened under the project; completion and current operation not confirmed (pre-2020, still_current null). Whether the 2017 EC$1.3m cheque is part of the US$2.5m sum is unclear. Hardware vendors not named.

findings.local_actor: Government Information and Technology Services Ltd (GITS); Ministry of the Public Service
findings.financier: TaiwanICDF (US$3.2m) with Government of Saint Lucia counterpart funds
findings.summary: Taiwan's ICDF financed the Government Island-wide Network (GINet), a public wireless network of 63 hotspots at 33 locations; by April 2017 equipment had shipped and operations-centre gear was installed at GITS.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: equipment vendor not named, so the controller under the equipment rule is unknown. Coded because it is a Taiwan-financed state network in a Taiwan-recognising state. Tier 4 as equipment delivered and partly installed; completion (due end 2018) not confirmed.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchases surfaced and none plausible at this scale

models.null_reason: one AI-partnership search found only a 2024 AI summit announcement and UNDP items; no model-provider partnership or national model

research_gaps: Confirm the CCTV camera manufacturer independently of MIGA (OLIX-branded models in the 2023 government consultancy) and whether the ~970 cameras are live, who hosts footage, and any analytics/ANPR software vendor.
Radio/core vendors for Digicel Saint Lucia and Flow's RAN (Flow 4G LTE launched 2017) not established.
Taiwan's 2023 grant included CCTV and security access systems for ministries; vendors not named.
Status of the Multi-Channel Data Centre and GINet: completed, operational, and whose hardware?
